doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: Mother's piano teaching, sheet music and Vince Mendoza
summary: She learned pop songs at the piano, read sheet music from her classical-pianist mother, and recalls Vince Mendoza on music that finds you.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

Did you sit at the piano with records and poke out the bass parts and then work out the chords to some of these songs?

Yeah. For pop songs definitely. I also read sheet music because my mother was a classical piano teacher and she didn’t understand the aural concept at all. And it wasn’t her fault and I actually feel for her because I think she really, in another life she wanted to be a jazz musician. Do you know what I mean? She was just on a quest all the time. There was music that made her feel good. Well you know when it makes you feel good I guess is the sort of driving underneath it all for me. What makes me go wow, I just want to listen to that again and figure it out. And unfortunately I’m a very — I have very close friends that are musicians, it’s mostly men, that are really great buddies of mine and I’ll sit there and they’ll go, “Isn’t this amazing?” And I’m like, “No I’m just not hearing what you’re hearing.” And mostly it’s because I was never into vocals. I was never into the poetry of the word. I was too transfixed with the melodies and the harmonies and the rhythms that the vocal part just got completely sidelined. And now I’m really into it so it’s okay. It just took me a long time. You know? But I think that if you meet all these great instrumental musicians, they kind of — again our lens has been trained a certain way. I think classical piano does it to you too, or classical lessons of some sort, that train you into really hearing the — visualizing the rhythm and the harmony much more so, so it distracts, but not in a bad way. It fed me lots of ideas. But The Police, I can’t sing every lyric but they did catch me a lot on the lyric to the point where I was doing that repetitive thing that kids do when they just listen to something over and over and they can’t stop listening. And how can you do that with jazz you know, like that’s kind of cool.
Yeah The Police were on my top five band list as well.

Yeah. I studied with Vince Mendoza slightly and he rings true when he goes, “Now there’s music you listened to but there’s also music that found you,” or “you didn’t find it, it found you” and then he played this amazing list of music that covers a very broad spectrum of classical, jazz and pop. And it’s really — it made me think and go you know that is what is the building blocks for you as a musician, whether you’re a composer or a player there’s these building blocks that land on us and we have to just find the right space for them to go and then move on to all this other stuff.
